newsitem.title: UK: BHP sees 30,000 bpd UK Lennox restarting in a mont.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees 30,000 bpd UK Lennox restarting in a mont.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty (BHP) said on Thursday it planned to restart oil production from its Lennox oilfield west of Britain in about a month's time.
Technical problems forced the field, which delivers crude ashore via the neighbouring Douglas platform, to close down after coming onstream in the middle of last year.
"We're now looking at the right moment to bring Lennox back onstream and the likely time frame is in about a month's time," said a BHP spokesman.
At full capacity Lennox would pump some 30,000 bpd combined with 40,000 bpd of Douglas, he said.
Meanwhile, the company was continuing twice a month to flush the pipeline carrying waxy Douglas crude to the terminal at Liverpool Bay.
The company is installing pipeline heaters to treat the problem of wax build-up and hopes the less waxy Lennox stream will reduce wax content.
